message: Makes me think, too, of work on sociolects in the US. Class becomes trappings, affectation: we buy our flannel and Chuck Taylors because, ya know, it's *authentic*. Or we buy a $300 blazer from J. Crew because gee, maybe it'll look like we went to Exeter, or that we're in Bloom's class at Yale. Fits right in there with the post after this one--we buy working class cred, the very act of which is a reinscription of our non-working-class-ness. Always reaching, occasionally grasping: this seems the real nature of the middle class.
